liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer calls the China Cat into Rider, The Other One and Jack Straw first-rate, huge-sounding music, with Jerry and Bob's effects notable [23]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The opening chord of Bertha gave the attendee an overwhelming sense of joy and loss of self-consciousness [24]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-12-30 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t02 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t03 Good Lovin'**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t04 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t05 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t06 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t07 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]
- **gd89-12-30 s1t08 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-12-30.142692.fob.schoeps.cmc3.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 171 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1989-12-30.165033.mtx.seamons.ht160.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 163 min [3]. Said about its sound: Clicks were removed in several songs, a 2-second soundboard cut in West L.A. Fadeaway was patched, and some scratchy claps remain [3]
- **gd89-12-30sbd.gardner.9754.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 29 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer complains Jerry's voice is shot and the piano tinkles; finds little psychedelic jamming and prefers pre-1978 music; Reviewer rebuts that Brent plays organ, not a tinkling piano, citing Bertha, and says Keith's piano sound was tinklier [19][20]
- **gd1989-12-30.sbd.ultramatrix.harrison.braverman.9122.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 160 min [7]

## Around the show

- Attendee, who went to about 20 shows, felt an ecstatic release of anxiety from Bertha's first chord; Airto's screams were grating [24]
- Airto played on and off throughout the show; the encore was It's All Over Now Baby Blue [4]
- Airto Moreira plays on Sugaree into West LA in the first set [7]
- Reviewer says the show was overshadowed by the next night's New Year's Eve show, but its versions rank among the best of the late 80s [18]
- Reviewer says they have never heard this early-era riff in any other 1980s or 1990s China Cat [22]
- Reviewer argues 1989-90 was among the Dead's best period, and this show demonstrates it against claims of decline after 1975-78 [23]
- Reviewer argues each era of the band deserves its own judgment, noting Jerry's peaks grew less obvious through the 80s and 90s [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-12-30.142692.fob.schoeps.cmc3.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master (FOB)Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC3/MK4 mics > Aerco PreAmp (w/ Oade capacitor mod)> Panasonic SV-250 (16-bit/48k);… [1]
- **gd1989-12-30.165033.mtx.seamons.ht160.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) July… [3]
- **gd89-12-30sbd.gardner.9754.sbeok.shnf**: source: Tony G shntool fix of original Braverman seed [5]
- **gd1989-12-30.sbd.ultramatrix.harrison.braverman.9122.shnf**: transferred by Rob Harrison performed the DAT>CD transfer; source: Ultramatrix (SBD/AUD mix) [7]. Also: Uploader traded for supposed Matrix copies several times over two years, but each had an audience-recorded second set [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 31, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/december-31-1989) [31]
